standard.title: Initiate exchanges and respond to questions
standard.description: initiate exchanges and respond to questions about home and classroom environments, using familiar expressions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interact in classroom routines, personal introductions and collaborative activities using modelled expressions (AC9LCH2C01, AC9LCH2C02). They can make polite requests, express thanks and preferences. They have not yet independently initiated exchanges, maintained multi-turn conversations, asked for clarification, or used digital communication formats in the target language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate exchanges and respond to questions about home and classroom environments using familiar expressions — including initiating and sustaining multi-turn conversations, seeking clarification, and using digital formats for interaction.

nodes.label: Initiating and sustaining conversations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate a conversation by asking a question in a familiar context and sustain it through at least three turns, using appropriate turn-taking strategies.
nodes.minimum_width: Initiate at least one exchange by asking an opening question and sustain it for at least three turns, using at least one turn-taking strategy (suggestion, follow-up question, or response to a peer's question).
nodes.typical_width: Initiate conversations in different contexts by asking questions about familiar topics — home, school, interests, daily routines; maintain exchanges by taking turns, making suggestions and responding to peers; use emoticons or digital conventions in appropriate digital communication contexts.
wider: Initiate and sustain a conversation on a topic introduced by the partner — demonstrate flexibility in responding to an unexpected topic direction
Compare conversation initiation conventions in the target language with English — identify different ways of opening a conversation and what makes each appropriate
nodes.hinge_reason: Initiating exchanges is the entry condition for all subsequent interaction development. Students who can only respond to teacher-led prompts cannot participate in the peer-to-peer and student-led exchanges that the Y3-4 and Y5-6 descriptors require.

response_modes.reason: Conversation initiation requires a growing bank of opening questions and turn-taking strategies across different topics and contexts. Repeated practice across varied familiar topics — not only one scripted exchange — builds the flexible initiation capacity that the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Initiates at least one exchange with an opening question appropriate to the context
Sustains the exchange for at least three turns without teacher prompting

nodes.label: Asking for clarification and seeking help
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can ask for clarification during an exchange and seek advice or help using appropriate formulaic expressions and gesture.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one clarification request and one help-seeking expression correctly in context.
nodes.typical_width: Ask for clarification using appropriate formulaic expressions and gestures; seek advice or help in appropriate contexts; recognise when to ask for clarification and select the appropriate form; use clarification requests to sustain rather than abandon an exchange.
wider: Compare how clarification is requested in the target language with English — identify where the conventions are similar and where they differ
Role-play a scenario where a communication breakdown occurs and model the use of clarification strategies to repair the exchange

response_modes.reason: Clarification and help-seeking are strategies needed across all interaction contexts — peer exchange, guest speaker interaction, transactional scenarios. Practising these strategies across varied contexts builds confident, flexible deployment.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Clarification and repair strategies are marks of sophisticated communicative competence. Width investment here builds the interactional resilience that allows students to sustain exchanges in unfamiliar or challenging contexts — a capability that distinguishes fluent from fragile interaction.
success_criteria: Uses at least one clarification request appropriately during an exchange
Uses at least one help-seeking expression in an appropriate context

nodes.label: Digital and written interaction formats
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create short texts in digital or written formats to interact with others — inviting, congratulating, thanking or sharing information — using appropriate format conventions.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least one short interactive text (email, letter, message, or invitation) using appropriate format conventions and at least three target language phrases.
nodes.typical_width: Create short texts in digital and written formats — emails, letters, text messages, invitations — to interact with others; use appropriate conventions for different formats; share information about school, community or personal experiences through written interaction.
wider: Compare the conventions of a formal and an informal written or digital interaction in the target language — identify what changes (greeting, closing, vocabulary, register) and explain why
Create a digital interaction text for a specific purpose and audience — for example, a message to a peer in a target language community — selecting format and language appropriately

response_modes.reason: Digital and written interaction integrates initiation skills (node 1) and clarification/help-seeking strategies (node 2) into a different mode — written production for a genuine communicative purpose. The teaching investment is in making the format conventions explicit and in creating real or realistic interaction partners.

success_criteria: Creates a short interactive text using at least three target language phrases and appropriate format conventions
The text has a clear communicative purpose — invitation, thanks, or information sharing
